boilerplate.section_intro: This section consists of questions and problems involving quantitative reasoning.  Each question is followed by four possible responses.  Choose the correct answer and mark its number in the appropriate place on the answer sheet.
boilerplate.section_meta:
This section contains 20 questions.
The time allotted is 20 minutes.
boilerplate.gray_note: Note:  The words appearing against a gray background are translated into several languages at the bottom of each page.
boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro:
Study the graph below, then answer the four questions that follow.

The graph presents data on the final exams of five students in a certain course.  All the exams were administered in the same month.
Each of the students was entitled to be tested more than once.  The final grade in the course is the grade that the student received on his last exam.
Each symbol in the graph indicates an exam of a student (see key).  The position of each of the symbols indicates the day in the month on which the exam was administered (the horizontal axis) and the student's grade on that exam (the vertical axis).  Next to each symbol is written the number of hours that the student studied for the exam.

For example: On the 10th of the month Boaz was tested for the second time.  He studied 10 hours for this exam, and his grade on the exam was 70.

Study the graph below, then answer the four questions that follow. The graph describes data regarding the height of men in a certain city. The height of all the men in the city is in the range between 150 cm and 210 cm. This range is divided into 8 height groups, and each height group is marked in the graph by a rectangle. The position of the rectangle on the horizontal axis represents the range of heights of the members of the group. The number of small squares that the rectangle contains (including parts of squares) represents the percentage of the men, out of all the men in the city, who belong to this group. Each whole small square represents 1% of the men in the city. For example: In the 170-175 cm height group there are 10 whole squares, 10 half squares, \(\frac{2}{3}\) of a square and \(\frac{1}{3}\) of a square. This means that the height of 16% of the men in the city is between 170 and 175 cm.

AB is a diameter in a circle whose center is O.
Based on this information and the information in the figure,

α + β = ?

methods.text: \((a+b)(b-a)\) is the difference of squares with the terms in the other order: it equals \(b^2-a^2\).
Take \(a=1, b=3\): the product is \(4 \times 2 = 8\), and \(b^2-a^2 = 8\). The squared options give 4 and 4, and the sum gives 10.

questions.stem:
In a certain raffle a monetary prize is raffled off, and it is divided equally among the winners.  If two participants win, each one of them will receive a sum that is greater by 150,000 shekels than the sum that each one of them would receive if they were to divide the prize with a third winner.

What is the size of the total prize (in shekels)?

Given: a is equal to 20% of b.
     b is equal to x% of a.

x = ?

methods.text: Set \(b = 100\), so \(a = 20\). Then \(b\) as a percentage of \(a\) is \(\frac{100}{20} = 500\%\).
The reverse of “20% of” is “500% of”, the reciprocal. Option (1) subtracts from 100 and option (4) is \(\frac{1}{0.25}\) — both are the wrong operation.

questions.stem:
The angles of a triangle satisfy the ratio 3:1:1 between them.

Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
options: All the angles of the triangle are acute
The triangle has a right angle
The triangle has an obtuse angle
None of the above statements is necessarily true

questions.stem:
In the accompanying figure the point O is the center of the base of the cone.  AO is the height of the cone.

Based on this information and the information in the figure,
what is the volume of the cone (in cm³)?

In a classroom there are 4 rows of chairs, and in each row there are 3 chairs.
Daniella and Maya enter the classroom and want to sit in two chairs that are adjacent to each other in the same row.

In how many ways can they do this?

Rafi, Naomi and Yoav each prepared a cup of coffee:
Rafi used \(\frac{1}{2}\) a teaspoon of coffee and 1 teaspoon of sugar,
Naomi used \(1\frac{1}{2}\) teaspoons of coffee and \(1\frac{1}{2}\) teaspoons of sugar,
and Yoav used 1 teaspoon of coffee only.

What is the ratio between the number of all the teaspoons of coffee and the number of all the teaspoons of sugar that they used to prepare the cups of coffee?

methods.text: Total coffee is \(\frac12 + 1\frac12 + 1 = 3\); total sugar is \(1 + 1\frac12 = 2\frac12\). The ratio is \(3 : 2.5 = 6:5\).
Yoav used no sugar at all, so he contributes to one total only. Reading each person's contribution to each total separately is the whole task.

questions.stem: Which of the following students was tested on two consecutive exams with a difference of more than 12 days?

The teacher decided to change the method of calculating the final grade in the course.  She determined that the final grade would be the highest grade that the student received on the final exams of the course.

The final grade of which of the following students would change as a result of the teacher's decision?

Due to technical problems it became clear that all the exams that were administered on Fridays in this month must be checked again.
The 1st of the month described in the graph fell on a Friday.

How many exams were checked again in this month?

A student begins to study for the second exam on the same day on which the first exam was administered, and continues until the day before the second exam (including the day before the exam).

Which of the following students studied an average of two hours a day for his second exam?

In a television quiz show n participants won a free trip abroad (2 < n). Each of the participants who won chose at random a destination country from a list of (n – 1) countries. Which of the following statements is necessarily true regarding the countries on the list?
options: At least one participant travelled to every country
At most 2 participants travelled to every country
There is at least one country to which no participant travelled
There is at least one country to which at least 2 participants travelled

methods.text: \(x + y = \frac{1}{3z}\), so \(y = \frac{1-3zx}{3z}\) and, taking the reciprocal, \(\frac1y = \frac{3z}{1-3zx}\).
The question asks for \(\frac1y\), not \(y\) — so isolate \(y\) as a single fraction first and flip once at the end, rather than trying to invert term by term.

questions.stem:
a, b and c are integers.
Given: b = a+2
     c = b+2

Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
options: a · b · c is divisible by 4 without a remainder
b · (a+c) is divisible by 3 without a remainder
c · (a+b) is divisible by 3 without a remainder
a+b+c is divisible by 3 without a remainder

methods.text: With \(b = a+2\) and \(c = a+4\), the sum is \(3a + 6 = 3(a+2)\) — always a multiple of 3.
The other options fail on \(a=1\): \(a \cdot b \cdot c = 15\) is not divisible by 4, and \(b(a+c) = 3 \times 6 = 18\) is divisible by 3 but \(c(a+b) = 5 \times 4 = 20\) is not.

questions.stem:
n is a two-digit number.  If we subtract from it the sum of its digits, we will get the sum of its digits.

What is the tens digit of n ?

methods.text: \(n = 10t + u\) and the condition is \(10t + u - (t+u) = t + u\), that is \(9t = t + u\), so \(8t = u\). The only digit solution is \(t = 1,\ u = 8\).

Subtracting the digit sum from a two-digit number always leaves \(9t\) — a multiple of 9. So the question is really asking when \(9t\) equals the digit sum, and \(9t\) grows far too fast for more than one answer.

A bus driver travels back and forth between stations A and B. The trip lasts 30 minutes in each direction. Every time that the driver arrives at A or at B he rests for 10 minutes, and then continues travelling. It is known that at 9:00 the driver was on his way from A to B. It is not possible that at 10:00 the driver was -

questions.stem:
In a certain toy store, for every purchase of two toys a discount of 40% is given on the cheaper toy of them.
Menachem bought two toys in the store whose prices, before the discount, were 40 shekels and 50 shekels.

How much did Menachem pay for the toys (in shekels)?

methods.text: The discount applies to the cheaper toy, so 40% comes off the 40-shekel toy: \(40 \times 0.6 = 24\), plus 50 for the other. Total 74.
Applying the discount to the 50 toy instead gives 70, which is option (3) — the error the question is built to catch.
Add the two equations: the \(2y\) and \(-2y\) cancel and the constants give \(6x = 12\), so \(x = 2\).
The two equations are identical apart from the sign on 5 and on \(2y\), which is the signal that adding them will eliminate \(y\) outright.

questions.stem: In an office-supplies store a pencil costs 3 shekels, an eraser costs 6 shekels and a pen costs 12 shekels. Yoel bought pencils, erasers and pens in the store (at least one item of each kind). Which of the following numbers cannot be the price that Yoel paid for all the items that he bought (in shekels)?

Tap A pours water at a rate of 6 liters per minute, and tap B pours water at a rate of \(\frac{1}{2}\) a liter per minute. They begin to pour water into a bucket whose volume is 15 liters from tap A only. After 20 seconds they open tap B and now water flows into the bucket from both taps. After how much time from the moment of the beginning of the flow of the water will the bucket fill up?

methods.text: Multi-phase accounting. Tap A alone for 20 seconds delivers 2 litres, leaving 13.
Both taps give \(6.5\) litres a minute, so 13 litres takes exactly 2 minutes — total 2 minutes 20 seconds. Convert the 20 seconds to \(\frac13\) minute before using it.

questions.stem:
Given: \(y = \frac{2x^3}{3x^2}\) ,  2 < x < 3

What is the exact range of y ?

methods.text: \(y = \dfrac{2x^3}{3x^2} = \dfrac{2x}{3}\). On \(2<x<3\) that runs from \(\frac43\) to 2.

Take \(x = 2.5\), which lies in the given range: \(y = \frac{2(15.625)}{3(6.25)} = \frac{5}{3}\). That value falls inside \(\frac43 < y < 2\) and outside all three other ranges, so one substitution settles it.
The endpoints alone settle it: substituting \(x=2\) and \(x=3\) gives \(\frac43\) and 2, and only option (2) has those two bounds.

The height of how many men in the city is between 185 and 190 cm?

To which height group does this man belong?

The men belonging to the two groups whose members' height is between 180 cm and 190 cm were divided into three new groups:
180 - \(183\frac{1}{3}\) cm ,  \(183\frac{1}{3}\) - \(186\frac{2}{3}\) cm ,  \(186\frac{2}{3}\) - 190 cm.

Which of the following parts of graphs could describe these three new groups?

In the accompanying figure ABCD is a rhombus.
Given: AC = 1 cm
     BD = 2 cm

Based on this information, what is the perimeter of rhombus ABCD (in cm)?

In the accompanying table all the letters represent positive numbers.  The letters x, y and z represent the numbers obtained from multiplying the values of the column and the corresponding row.
For example: x = b · b

z = ?
options: It is impossible to express z with the help of x and y alone

methods.text: Each cell is the product of its row and column heading, so \(x = b^2\), \(y = c^2\) and \(z = bc\). Then \(xy = b^2c^2 = (bc)^2 = z^2\), so \(z = \sqrt{xy}\).
Give the headings values: \(b=2\) and \(c=3\) make \(x = 4\), \(y = 9\) and \(z = 6\). Then \(\sqrt{xy} = \sqrt{36} = 6\) matches, while \(\frac{x+y}{2} = 6.5\) and \(y-x = 5\) do not.
\(z\) is the geometric mean of \(x\) and \(y\), not the arithmetic one — which is what option (1) offers and what makes it the natural wrong answer.

questions.stem: It is not possible that two positive numbers, s and t, satisfy the equation -

methods.text: \(s + t = s - t\) forces \(2t = 0\), so \(t = 0\) — impossible for a positive number. The other three all have positive solutions.
Witnesses for the rest: \(s=t=2\) satisfies \(st = s+t\); \(s=4, t=2\) satisfies \(\frac st = s-t\); \(s=2, t=\frac23\) satisfies \(s-t = st\). Three examples close the question.

questions.stem:
Given: \(2^7 \cdot 3^2 \cdot x = 8!\)

x = ?

methods.text: Prime-factorise \(8!\) rather than computing it. \(8!=8\cdot7\cdot6\cdot5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot2\), which contributes \(2^{3+1+2+1}=2^7\), \(3^{1+1}=3^2\), one 5 and one 7. So \(8!=2^7\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7\), and dividing by \(2^7\cdot3^2\) leaves \(5\cdot7=35\).

The given hands you most of \(8!\)'s prime factorisation and asks what is left over. Whatever primes appear in \(8!\) but not on the left must be in \(x\) — and the only primes up to 8 not already listed are 5 and 7.

questions.stem:
Given: a + b + c = 0

Which of the following equations is necessarily true?

methods.text: \(a+b+c=0\) rearranges to \(a=-(b+c)\). A number and its negative have the same absolute value, so \(|a|=|b+c|\).
The other three would need the signs of \(b\) and \(c\), which the given never supplies. Only the identity that follows from rearranging survives.
\(a=1,\ b=2,\ c=-3\): \(|a|=1\) and \(|b+c|=1\) ✓, while \(|b-c|=5\), \(|b|+|c|=5\) and \(|b|-|c|=-1\) — all three wrong on a single test set.
